draft.title: Determinants and matrix equations
card: For a 2 × 2 matrix A with rows (a b) and (c d), the determinant is det(A) = ad − bc.
A square matrix has an inverse only if its determinant is not 0. If det(A) = 0, there is no inverse.
When det(A) = D is not 0, the inverse A⁻¹ is 1/D times the matrix with rows (d −b) and (−c a).
To solve AX = B, multiply both sides on the left by A⁻¹. This gives X = A⁻¹B. The order matters: A⁻¹ goes before B.
draft.remember: No inverse if det = 0. Otherwise X = A⁻¹B, with A⁻¹ on the left.

a.q: Matrix A has rows (3 2) and (4 5). What is det(A)?
a.why: det(A) = ad − bc = 3×5 − 2×4 = 15 − 8 = 7. The answer 23 comes from adding the products instead of subtracting.
a.clue: Main diagonal product, take away the other.

b.q: For which value of k does the matrix with rows (2 k) and (6 3) have no inverse?
b.why: det = 2×3 − 6k = 6 − 6k. There is no inverse when this is 0, so k = 1. The value k = 9 does not give 0, since 6 − 54 = −48.

final.title: Determinants and matrix equations
card: For a \(2 \times 2\) matrix \(A\) with rows \((a \quad b)\) and \((c \quad d)\), the determinant is \(\text{det}(A) = ad - bc\).
A square matrix has an inverse only if its determinant is not 0. If \(\text{det}(A) = 0\), there is no inverse.
When \(\text{det}(A) = D\) is not 0, the inverse \(A^{-1}\) is \(\frac{1}{D}\) times the matrix with rows \((d \quad -b)\) and \((-c \quad a)\).
To solve \(AX = B\), multiply both sides on the left by \(A^{-1}\). This gives \(X = A^{-1}B\). The order matters: \(A^{-1}\) goes before \(B\).
final.remember: No inverse if \(\text{det} = 0\). Otherwise \(X = A^{-1}B\), with \(A^{-1}\) on the left.

a.q: Matrix \(A\) has rows \((3 \quad 2)\) and \((4 \quad 5)\). What is \(\text{det}(A)\)?
a.why: \(\text{det}(A) = ad - bc = 3 \times 5 - 2 \times 4\), which is \(15 - 8 = 7\). The answer 23 comes from adding the products instead of subtracting.
a.clue: Main diagonal product, take away the other.

b.q: For which value of \(k\) does the matrix with rows \((2 \quad k)\) and \((6 \quad 3)\) have no inverse?
b.why: \(\text{det} = 2 \times 3 - 6k = 6 - 6k\). There is no inverse when this is 0, so \(k = 1\). The value \(k = 9\) does not give 0, since \(6 - 54 = -48\).
